questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I saw it as an incredible opportunity to live in a country so far away: Australia. I chose Melbourne because I have heard that the city and university are very international, which makes it easier for an exchange student.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can really recommend going on exchange. It is an amazing experience and an opportunity to meet people from all over the world and get another perspective on the field you study. The reason why I am not rating my study experience as a 10 is that I was not aware of all the work I had to do before leaving regarding the exchange program both here in Copenhagen but also in Melbourne. Further, it can be difficult to study in another country, where everything is different from home, and it is therefore a challenge you need to be prepared for.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: That was very easy, I think the University of Melbourne was very good at sending emails and contacting us if they needed more information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of emails with directions for what to do regarding my subjects etc. and further, they had this amazing help support team, called 'Stop 1', where I came the first day with many questions, and they were so helpful. Stop 1 is a help centre that is located on campus and is open all semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance and orientation was excellent.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it was a lot harder than I thought it would be. It was hard finding local apartments and all accommodation opportunities were very expensive. I ended up finding student accommodation together with some other Danes very close to the university, almost on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to meet up with other Danes from the University of Copenhagen before leaving and find accommodation together. And if you prefer living more locally without other Danes, I will recommend searching on sites as 'Flatmates' before your arrival. That was where some of the others found good accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was too expensive... We got discount because we were so many Danes booking it together, but it still costed 700 AUD dollars every second week..

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was good and the staff was very helpful. However, their system is a lot different from ours, so it is only possible to see the class hours when you have applied for a subject, and then if all the subjects overlap you need to apply for a new subject and get it approved by the University of Copenhagen etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registrated for subjects before going, and it was easy. But when arriving a lot of my subjects overlapped, so I needed to change several subjects. It was very easy to do at University of Melbourne, but it took a long time to get the subjects approved from University of Copenhagen before I could choose them in Melbourne.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 was the best help regarding this! Here you can book an appointment and get one-on-one help. There is also a room where you can stay with your computer and fix things while staff is walking around ready to help you, when you need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up having all the classes I wanted and was so happy for them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Research, research, research. It would have helped me a lot if I have searched some more on their website and found all the possible subjects that were available for me, so I know all the opportunities I had before going.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was quite high at post-graduate level but quite low at undergraduate level compared to the level at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two undergraduate level 3 subjects and two post-graduate level subjects. That was perfect in terms of work load.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is very similar to seminars at UCPH with a mix of presentation and class discussion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Migration and Development
Survey Design and Analysis
Contemporary Social Problems
Contemporary Sociological Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend all the subjects I have listed above. So good teachers and interesting stuff. And the exams were all essays, which I think was nice, then I was not required to stay in Melbourne doing the exam period.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Study visa (3120 kr)
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) - the minimum level of health insurance required for students traveling to Australia (1844 kr)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, insurance and food were much more expensive, but transportation, books, and communication were less expensive. Overall, it is just expensive to travel in Australia as well, so if you are planning on travelling before, during or after your exchange program, you should expect to use a lot on personal spending :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many clubs :)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All you can think of. Dance club, football club, mountaineering club, surf club, diving club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend the mountaineering club which I was a part of - a great way to experience what is around Melbourne and meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a uber car in the weekends and go see Great Ocean Road. Go to the Grampians. Go to Wilson Prom. And if you have more time during the break, travel up the east or west coast in a camper! :))

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Melbourne reminds me of Copenhagen a lot :)) in a very nice way

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the different clubs that campus offers.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were non. Only Australians can be just as closed as us Danes, so you maybe need to try a little harder than in other countries.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their coffee, café, bar and museum culture - these opportunities are amazing in Melbourne!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring all kinds of clothes - both warm and cold, you will need it. Bring cozy things like Danish flags and pictures of your friends and family for your room. Choose your subjects wisely.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a lot of scholarships so that you are able to travel all over Australia at the weekends and breaks. This is the only thing I regret - not bringing enough money :))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely, the output I got from my subjects - I am more motivated for studying than ever before. And all the great friends (mostly Danish people) I got. A lot like half a year at højskole.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That they have mid-term exams at the University of Melbourne - many of the first exams are 40% and then the rest are 60%. You need to adjust so you do not give 100% in all exams, otherwise, it is way too hard and you end up using too much time on studying in stead of enjoying your exchange, meeting people and experiencing the city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Look forward to a semester of crazy good Fitzroy vibes (similar to Nørrebro, Nordvest, and Berlin), amazing coffee, and the nicest people everywhere you go!! So friendly! And lastly, a top-class university.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
